html:
Radama I was king of Madagascar from 1810 to 1828, the son of Andrianampoinimerina, who made the Merina kingdom a modern state with British help.

In treaties of 1817 and 1820 he agreed with Britain to stop the export of slaves in return for weapons, training and money, and Britain recognised him as king of Madagascar. With a European-drilled army he conquered much of the east and the Sakalava lands.

He welcomed missionaries of the London Missionary Society, who opened schools from 1818 and with his approval wrote the Malagasy language in the Latin alphabet. Many officials learned to read, which made Madagascar one of the first African states with a literate government. His widow Ranavalona I reversed much of his policy toward the Christian missions.
